data.title: Shriram Finance To Replace Trent In BSE Sensex From 21 December
data.description:
The latest BSE index reshuffle will also see Divi’s Laboratories replace Wipro in the Sensex 50, while five companies each will be added to and removed from the BSE 100

Shriram Finance will replace Trent in the 30-stock BSE Sensex from 21 December, following a reconstitution of several benchmark indices announced by BSE Index Services on Friday.

The changes, which will take effect at the opening of trading on 21 December, will also affect the BSE 100, BSE Sensex 50, BSE Sensex Next 50, BSE Sensex Next 30 and BSE Focused IT indices.

Changes In Key Indices

In the BSE Sensex 50, Divi’s Laboratories will replace information technology services company Wipro. The BSE 100 will see five additions and five exclusions. Multi Commodity Exchange of India (MCX), Vedanta Aluminium Metal, Laurus Labs, Bharat Heavy Electricals (BHEL) and GE Vernova T&D India will enter the index.

They will replace Punjab National Bank, Godrej Consumer Products, SRF, Shree Cement and Havells India, respectively. The BSE Sensex Next 50 will also undergo six changes. MCX, Vedanta Aluminium Metal, Laurus Labs, BHEL, GE Vernova T&D India and Wipro will be included, replacing Divi’s Laboratories, Havells India, Godrej Consumer Products, Shree Cement, SRF and Punjab National Bank.

Rejig Across Other Indices

The BSE Sensex Next 30 will see Trent, Adani Power, Federal Bank, MCX and Cummins India enter the index. They will replace Britannia Industries, HDFC Life Insurance, Suzlon Energy, Wipro and Shriram Finance.

In the BSE Focused IT index, Sagility will replace L&T Technology Services. The BSE Bankex will remain unchanged in the latest review.

The periodic reconstitution of indices is intended to ensure that their composition reflects changes in market representation, liquidity and free-float market capitalisation. Such changes can also require index-tracking funds and exchange-traded funds to realign their portfolios.

data.title: IoTeX Opened Voting on IIP-65 Bunker Mode
data.description:
IoTeX opened voting on IIP-65, “Bunker Mode”, on November 21st at 00:00 UTC; voting will continue until November 28th at 00:00 UTC. The proposal would add an optional SLH-DSA guard key to staked IOTX, preventing withdrawals, transfers and voting changes without that key while staking rewards continue.

Refer to the official tweet by IOTX:

IoTeX
@iotex_io

Voting on IIP-65: Bunker Mode 🛡ï¸ opens today at 4pm PT (00:00 UTC, Nov 21).

Nobody knows when a quantum computer, or an AI-assisted math breakthrough, will break the ECDSA keys that protect crypto today. Upgrading every account to post-quantum needs exchanges, wallets andâ€¦

Nov 20, 2026

IOTX Info

IoTeX (IOTX) is an open-source blockchain platform specifically designed for the Internet of Things (IoT) with a strong emphasis on scalability, privacy, isolation, and the ability to develop decentralized applications and IoT ecosystems.

IoTeX was created to address the technical challenges faced by existing IoT ecosystems, such as security issues, high maintenance costs, and scalability limitations. The project is developing a new blockchain architecture to support a large number of IoT devices.

At the core of IoTeX is the concept of "blockchain within a blockchain." The main network, or "root blockchain," is responsible for network management and security, while internal blockchains, or "sub-blockchains," are used to manage various IoT devices and process transactions.

The IoTeX network utilizes its native token, IOTX, for operations such as transaction fee payments and participation in network governance.

data.title: BENQI to Introduce an sAVAX Unstaking Queue in November
data.description:
BENQI will update sAVAX unstaking in November, replacing the fixed 15-day wait with a queue following Avalanche’s Helicon upgrade. AVAX, including accrued rewards, could become available in as little as 48 hours or take up to 14 days during high demand; existing requests will carry over with elapsed waiting time preserved.

Refer to the official tweet by QI:

BENQI🔺
@BenqiFinance

2/2 Holding sAVAX? You donâ€™t need to move or swap it. Your sAVAX remains the same and still earns staking rewards automatically.

Already unstaking? Your request will carry over, and the time youâ€™ve already waited still counts. Once your AVAX is ready, you can claim it anytime.â€¦

Nov 20, 2026

QI Info

BENQI is a DeFi protocol developed on the Avalanche network, comprising two main components: BENQI Liquid Staking (BLS) and BENQI Liquidity Market (BLM). BLS provides a liquid staking solution for Avalanche, allowing users to earn yields on staked capital, while BLM facilitates a lending and borrowing environment for crypto-assets through smart contracts.

The operational mechanism of BENQI involves BLS, which enables users to stake with Avalanche validators and use the staked assets without lock-up periods. BLM, on the other hand, operates as a lending and borrowing protocol on the Avalanche network, allowing users to lend, borrow, and earn interest on their crypto assets. The protocol is fully automated through smart contracts, calculating yields algorithmically based on supply and demand, and enabling over-collateralized borrowing.

QI is the native token of BENQI, serving dual roles as a governance and utility token. It is essential for managing and voting on proposals within the BENQI DAO, influencing the protocol’s direction, including economic policies, security upgrades, and further development. Additionally, QI allows for staking, earning delegation rewards, and provides enhanced functionality within the BENQI ecosystem.

data.title: Anthropic's 20X Sales Valuation Makes Samsung And Hynix Look Like Bargains, Warns Dan Niles
data.description:
Key points:
  • Niles said that he attempted to short Anthropic after the stock surged roughly 30% following its IPO, but was unable to find shares available to borrow.
  • He noted that for him, the comparison comes down to how much investors are paying for exposure to the broader AI ecosystem and the risks embedded in those valuations.
  • Anthropic shares opened 34% higher on debut and finished the session up 17%, a performance Niles said was less convincing than the headline gains might suggest.

Anthropic's blockbuster IPO has put the artificial intelligence trade back in the spotlight, but veteran tech investor Dan Niles questioned whether investors are paying too steep a price for the AI startup's growth prospects.

During an interview with CNBC, Niles said he sees a stark valuation contrast between Anthropic and established semiconductor players like Samsung Electronics Co. Ltd. (SSNLF) and SK Hynix Inc. (SKHY), arguing that investors betting on AI may be overlooking more attractively priced opportunities elsewhere in the ecosystem.

Anthropic shares fell nearly 9% in Friday’s regular trading, declining over 1% more during the afterhours session.

Niles Says He Tried To Short ANT Stock As Its Shares Surged

Niles, founder of Niles Investment Management, said that he attempted to short Anthropic after the stock surged roughly 30% following its IPO, but was unable to find shares available to borrow.

"When it was up 30% yesterday, I went and tried to get a borrow to short it. There was none available. I tried, I tried again this morning to get a borrow to short it. There was none available," Niles said during an appearance on CNBC's Squawk on the Street on Thursday.

Niles questioned whether Anthropic's valuation justified the enthusiasm, contrasting the company's valuation with those of established semiconductor companies that are also benefiting from the AI infrastructure boom.

"You can buy it at 20 times trailing revenues or calendar 26 revenues, or you could go buy Samsung or Hynix at two times trailing earnings," he said.

Niles noted that for him, the comparison comes down to how much investors are paying for exposure to the broader AI ecosystem and the risks embedded in those valuations.

He emphasized that investing ultimately comes down to weighing potential returns against the risks involved, with valuations offering a crucial gauge of that balance.

Niles Questions Whether Anthropic's IPO Was As Successful As It Appeared

Anthropic's IPO initially appeared to deliver a strong debut, with shares opening substantially higher before giving back some of those gains by the close. Niles, however, argued that the intraday price action raised questions about the strength of demand relative to selling pressure.

The stock opened 34% higher and finished the session up 17%, a performance Niles said was less convincing than the headline gains might suggest.

"You can make an argument that the IPO did not go that great," Niles said.

While he acknowledged that the offering was positive for Anthropic itself because the company raised more money than expected, he pointed to the gap between the opening and closing gains as a potential warning sign.

"For a successful IPO you want to see it open and then continue to climb during the day," Niles said.

"It opened up 34%. It closed up 17. So what does that tell you?"

Niles said the price action suggested sellers were more aggressive at the open than buyers looking to enter the stock, raising doubts about whether Anthropic could sustain its IPO price.

"Clearly the sellers were more aggressive at the open versus anybody who wanted to step into it," he said.

Ultimately, Niles returned to the valuation question, arguing that investors need to weigh the price they are paying for AI exposure against alternatives in the semiconductor industry.

"If you don't want to buy Samsung at three times earnings, do you really want to buy this at 20 times sales? That's the problem."

What Retail Investors Think Of ANT Stock

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits around Anthropic trended in the ‘extremely bullish’ territory at the time of writing.

ANT stock is down 20% year-to-date. The S&P 500 ETF (SPY) is up 6% over the past 12 months, while the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) is up 4%.

data.description:
Star Atlas will deploy the SAGE C4 3.2 PTR update for its browser game Golden Era on November 21st. The update will revise Council research and career progression, add governance modules and voting at eligible starbases, and rebalance ship configurations, regional resources and crafting.

Refer to the official tweet by ATLAS:

Star Atlas
@staratlas

The single largest update to Star Atlas: Golden Era (browser), ever. Going live today.

SAGE C4 3.2 PTR â€” PATCH NOTES

Council progression, ship fitting, territorial governance, resource distribution, and more. The release review covered 390 pull requests.

COUNCIL RANK &â€¦ pic.twitter.com/tMrdf1CoGy

ATLAS Info

Star Atlas is an ambitious MMO game built on the Solana blockchain. It serves as a true metaverse, combining elements of strategy, exploration, and combat in a world filled with cosmic science fiction.

Star Atlas offers players the opportunity to explore space, mine resources, build ships and colonies, and engage in battles with other players. The in-game economy is based on cryptocurrencies, enabling players to earn real money through their participation in the game. Every action, from resource mining to construction and battles, can be tokenized and exchanged for real-world currency.

Star Atlas utilizes non-fungible tokens (NFTs) to create unique digital assets that can be traded on its in-game marketplace. These NFTs encompass a wide range of items, including spaceships and land plots on various planets.

By leveraging the scalability and low fees of the Solana blockchain, Star Atlas establishes a seamless, dynamic, and immersive gaming environment. Additionally, the project incorporates Unreal Engine 5 technology to craft a visually detailed game world.

The ATLAS token serves as the in-game currency within the Star Atlas metaverse. It is a cryptocurrency that players can utilize for various purposes within the game.

data.title: Gold made investors richer. But could their money have worked harder?
data.description:
Gold is one of the few assets Indians buy without first asking what it will return. We buy it for weddings, festivals and family security. For generations, it has symbolised wealth preservation and financial protection.

So, when gold prices rise sharply, it creates a perception that everyone holding gold has become wealthier. But there is a difference between an asset performing well and investors actually capturing those returns.

After an extraordinary rally followed by a sharp correction, three questions matter: When did investors buy gold? What drove returns in India? And what opportunities did they give up by choosing gold over other investments?

Gold went up. Did investors capture the rally?

Between March 2024 and October 2026, Gold ETFs attracted cumulative net inflows of Rs 1.01 lakh crore. Interestingly, nearly 50 percent came during 2026, after gold had already appreciated substantially.

To understand the impact, we compared actual investor cash flows with two hypothetical approaches involving the same cumulative investment of Rs 1,01,397 crore.

The annualised return on actual investor flows was just 15.50 percent. Investing a fixed amount every month would have delivered 29.70 percent, while investing the entire amount at the beginning would have generated 32.72 percent.

The difference is striking. Despite gold's extraordinary rally, investors captured considerably lower returns because of when they invested.

This reflects recency bias. Investors often become more comfortable buying an asset after watching its price rise. The lesson is not that lump sum investing always outperforms SIPs, but that investment decisions should follow a disciplined allocation strategy rather than recent performance.

Why does gold deliver different returns in India?

International gold prices are denominated in US dollars, but Indian households buy gold in rupees. Domestic returns, therefore, depend on global prices, currency movements and import duties.

Our analysis of the past 20 years shows that gold delivered average annual returns of 11.92 percent in dollar terms, compared with 16.05 percent in rupees. The 4.13 percentage-point difference is largely attributable to rupee depreciation.

A recent one-year period illustrates this particularly well. International gold prices declined 5.40 percent, yet Indian prices rose 10.23 percent. This divergence of 15.63 percentage points was largely driven by 7 percent rupee depreciation and an increase in customs duty from 6 percent to 15 percent.

But can this additional return continue indefinitely? Not necessarily. A stronger rupee or lower import duties could put pressure on domestic gold prices even if international prices remain unchanged.

What else could that money have earned?

The more interesting question is not just how much wealth gold created, but whether the same money could have earned more elsewhere.

Our analysis estimates that Indian households invested Rs 118.97 lakh crore in gold between 2013 and 2026. At November 2026 valuations, this would have grown to Rs 464.99 lakh crore.

However, investing the equivalent amount in the equity mutual fund basket used in our comparison would have generated Rs 554.42 lakh crore, nearly Rs 90 lakh crore more.

This does not mean households literally lost Rs 90 lakh crore. It is a hypothetical comparison. Gold bought for weddings, jewellery and family requirements serves purposes that equities cannot replace.

Nevertheless, it highlights an important distinction: earning positive returns is not necessarily the same as maximising wealth creation. Every investment choice carries an opportunity cost.

The recent correction: What has changed?

After an extraordinary rally, international gold prices have fallen nearly 31 percent from their January 2026 peak of $5,405 per ounce, while domestic prices have corrected 25 percent from Rs 1,75,231 per 10 grams.

Concerns over US inflation and tighter monetary policy have increased the attractiveness of interest-bearing investments. The US 10-year Treasury yield has crossed 5 percent, while a stronger dollar has added pressure on gold.

Investor behaviour has also contributed. Momentum-driven buying and leveraged positions during the rally gave way to profit booking and the unwinding of futures positions as prices declined.

Demand is moderating, too. Global jewellery consumption fell 17 percent year-on-year in Q3 2026, while Indian consumption declined 20 percent. Global Gold ETF inflows slowed from $10 billion in September to $2.7 billion in October.

The correction does not mean gold has lost its long-term relevance. But it reinforces a familiar lesson: past performance cannot be extrapolated indefinitely, and a sharp price decline does not automatically make an investment attractive.

Should gold be part of every investor's portfolio?

As a broad allocation framework, investors can consider allocating up to 50 percent of their debt allocation to gold, or 10–15 percent of their overall portfolio. Those already overweight on gold should consider rebalancing towards their strategic allocation rather than adding exposure simply because prices have corrected.

The objective of investing is not to own whichever asset has delivered the highest recent returns. It is to build a portfolio that offers the highest probability of achieving financial goals.

Ultimately, the real measure of wealth creation is not how brightly an asset shines, but how effectively it contributes to an investor's overall financial journey.

The author is the Joint CEO Anand Rathi Wealth Limited.

data.title: Vietnam passes law to speed up land expropriation for priority projects
data.description:
Key points:
  • Law aims to ease delays to infrastructure, industrial projects
  • Under new law expropriation decisions could be made before compensation determined

Vietnam's parliament approved a law on Saturday to speed up the expropriation of land in the case of some special projects, a move that could boost infrastructure development while reducing the leverage of farmers in fighting such seizures.

The legislation aims to ease delays to infrastructure and industrial projects in Vietnam, many of which have been held back by complaints from residents and farmers that compensation for expropriated land was below market value.

Under the revised land law, authorities may issue land-expropriation decisions before compensation plans are approved, provided no resettlement is required and the plans have been publicly disclosed.

The provision applies to nationally important projects, urgent public-investment projects, cases where more than 75% of affected land users agree to the expropriation.

"From a technical standpoint, the provision appears designed to facilitate timely implementation of priority projects while retaining procedural safeguards," said Chris Luong, a partner at CNC Counsel, a law firm specialising in construction, infrastructure and real estate.

Among the 479 National Assembly deputies, five opposed the revised land law and eight did not cast a vote. The law will be implemented from July 1, 2027.

The revised law introduces additional safeguards for people whose land is expropriated, including stronger resettlement protections, livelihood support for up to three years and expanded vocational training, Minister of Agriculture and Environment Trinh Viet Hung told parliament on Saturday.

Previously, compensation plans generally had to be approved before the land could be expropriated.

The change could be particularly relevant for agricultural land, where expropriation is less likely to require households to relocate, rather than in cases involving residential property, Luong said.

Application of the law would, however, still depend on the project type and the prescribed consent thresholds, he said.

Land disputes have long been a sensitive issue in Vietnam, where negotiations over compensation often drag on for years and ⁠occasionally ​trigger protests in the tightly controlled ​country.

In Hanoi, some residents living along the Red River earlier this year hung banners and marched through their neighbourhood urging authorities to reconsider a proposed $28 billion redevelopment plan that could affect about 280,000 people.

Another high-profile case involves a Trump Organization-backed golf project in northern Hung Yen province that includes farmland acquired from local residents.

Lawmakers said the revised law would also introduce clearer criteria for land acquisitions and reform the way land is valued with more transparent, data-driven pricing methods.

Lawmakers also passed a data security law expanding state oversight of sensitive data and cross-border data flows, and approved changes to the criminal code that remove the death penalty for six offences, including drug trafficking and child rape.

In Yokohama City Minato Mirai area new entertaining spot of Yamaha Motor appeared. Yamaha new E-RIDE BASE has launched. Visitors can enjoy experience of matching e-bike and animation game “Zenless Zone Zero”. “Zenless Zone Zero” is a global famous roleplaying game. Yamaha Motor says, “You can feel like a hero.”

Last year Yamaha Motor cooperated to TICAD (Tokyo International Conference on Africa Development). Special exhibition in the conference and E-RIDE BASE had gotten big fame. Sympathized African guests visited E-RIDE BASE.

Yamaha looks to global outreach

In next year Yokohama City will hold world conference of United Nations. Yamaha Motor will utilize this opportunity to introduce Yamaha policy.

Yamaha Motor considers sustainable clean environment and safe bike riding. New launching of E-RIDE BASE may contribute to send its policy all over the world.

data.title: LEPAS L8 PHEV Makes Its Gulf Debut, Bringing Elegant Mobility to the Middle East
data.description:
DUBAI, United Arab Emirates and WUHU, China, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- LEPAS, Chery Auto’s Premium NEV brand, officially entered the Gulf market with a regional brand launch in Dubai. Its first model in the region, the LEPAS L8, is now on sale in the UAE, starting at AED 99,999, with launches in Kuwait, Qatar and other markets to follow.

As the Gulf accelerates its transition to new energy mobility, policy support and interest in electrified vehicles continue to grow. Customers seek vehicles that combine distinctive design with the ability to handle diverse road and climate conditions. The LEPAS L8 PHEV meets these expectations as an Elegant All-round Premium SUV, bringing together refined design, confident driving and intelligent technology.

The first 100 customers will receive exclusive benefits, including insurance, maintenance and complimentary roadside assistance. LEPAS also offers a 7-year/200,000-km vehicle warranty and an 8-year/160,000-km warranty for the electric powertrain system, providing added peace of mind.

Elegant Design: Where Natural Energy Meets Spacious Comfort

Created for customers who appreciate bold design and refined details, the LEPAS L8 PHEV embodies Leopard Aesthetics, inspired by the agility and strength of the leopard. Flowing body lines and the distinctive Leaping Leopard Beltline create a dynamic sense of movement, while the Pioneering Leopard Avant-Garde Front Fascia and Leopard-Eye LED Headlights give the SUV a commanding yet expressive presence.

With a 2,800-mm wheelbase and 66.5% space utilization, the LEPAS L8 PHEV offers a spacious five-seat layout. Its wraparound cabin creates a welcoming atmosphere, complemented by Cloud Comfort Lounge Seats and excellent NVH performance for a quiet, comfortable ride. A 507L cargo capacity, 47 Ingenious Storage Spaces and versatile seating configurations make room for passengers and everyday essentials alike, turning the cabin into a comfortable living space on the move.

Elegant Driving: Smart Assistance Makes Journeys Easier

Built on the intelligent LEX Platform, the LEPAS L8 PHEV features APA and RPA Parking Assistance to simplify parking in busy urban environments, from maneuvering in tight spaces to parking in designated spaces in multi-level garages. Its 16 ADAS features also assist with following distance, lane keeping and hazard detection, making daily commutes and intercity journeys easier.

For greater awareness in busy streets and at turns with limited visibility, the LEPAS L8 PHEV features 540° Panoramic View. A cage-style body structure, six airbags and a battery pack with IP68 and IPX9K protection ratings provide additional layers of safety and reassurance.

Local Adaptation: Balancing Driving Efficiency with Everyday Needs

Powered by LEPAS Super Hybrid, the L8 PHEV balances energy efficiency with extended range for daily commutes and longer journeys. Under the NEDC test cycle, it delivers a combined range of up to 1,300 km and an all-electric range of more than 100 km, with charging from 30% to 80% taking just 20 minutes. Whether commuting or travelling beyond the city, customers can enjoy greater flexibility on the road.

The L8 PHEV is also adapted to the region’s hot climate. Its upgraded air-conditioning system, combined with UV-Blocking and Heat-Insulating Glass, helps keep the cabin cool under intense sunlight. Meanwhile, the AQS Air Quality Monitoring System monitors cabin air quality, ensuring a fresh and comfortable interior.

The L8 PHEV marks the beginning of LEPAS’s broader presence in the Middle East. More LEPAS NEV models will follow, expanding choices for local customers. The brand will also continue to co-create with customers across the region, drawing on diverse cultures and perspectives to shape new expressions of elegant living and bring its brand promise, “Drive Your Elegance,” to more people worldwide.

About LEPAS

LEPAS is Chery Auto's Premium NEV brand, dedicated to creating elegant mobility experiences for users worldwide. Committed to becoming the Preferred Brand for Elegant Mobility Life, LEPAS brings together Leopard Aesthetics, Elegant Technology, and Exquisite Space - transforming elegance into a driving experience you can see, feel, and trust. Supported by a growing global dealer network of more than 500 sales and service outlets, LEPAS is expanding its international footprint through localized operations, delivering products and experiences tailored to users across global markets.

About Chery Auto

Founded in 1997, Chery Auto is a global automotive manufacturer specializing in vehicle development, intelligent technologies, and new energy solutions. The company operates in more than 130 countries and regions, supported by a strong international network of research, production, and strategic partnerships. Chery Auto has remained China’s No. 1 passenger vehicle exporter among Chinese brands for 23 consecutive years. Guided by its global philosophy of "In somewhere, For somewhere, Be somewhere," Chery Auto is committed to advancing sustainable mobility through continuous innovation and global collaboration.

data.title: Peter Schiff Says Gold's $2,000 Pullback Could Be A Warning — 'Stocks Will Ultimately Fall Much Further'
data.description:
Key points:
  • Schiff pointed to gold's performance during the 2008 financial crisis, when the precious metal fell roughly 30% before bottoming in October that year.
  • He noted that stocks continued to tumble for months, with the S&P 500 eventually falling nearly 60% from its peak before bottoming in March 2009.
  • Schiff added that gold subsequently staged a massive recovery, rising 166% from its 2008 bottom to its 2011 peak and nearly doubling its previous 2008 high.

Gold's sharp retreat from its record highs may not be a reason for investors to panic, but rather a warning sign of a broader financial crisis ahead, according to economist and longtime gold bull Peter Schiff.

Drawing parallels with the 2008 financial crisis, Schiff argued in posts on X that gold could be repeating a familiar pattern in which the precious metal bottoms before stocks, potentially setting the stage for another major rally as equities continue to slide.

Schiff Sees A 2008 Repeat As Gold Falls Ahead Of Stocks

Schiff pointed to gold's performance during the 2008 financial crisis, when the precious metal fell roughly 30% before bottoming in October that year. He noted that stocks continued to tumble for months, with the S&P 500 eventually falling nearly 60% from its peak before bottoming in March 2009.

The economist added that gold subsequently staged a massive recovery, rising 166% from its 2008 bottom to its 2011 peak and nearly doubling its previous 2008 high, while stocks remained well below their pre-crisis levels.

Schiff believes a similar pattern could be unfolding again, only with a potentially more severe financial crisis ahead.

"Just like in 2008, gold is again falling first, but stocks will ultimately fall much further," Schiff said.

He added that stocks could continue falling even after gold reverses higher, with the precious metal potentially reaching fresh record highs while equities remain significantly below their previous peaks.

Spot gold prices fell 2.41% to $3,538 per ounce on Friday.

Schiff Says Debt And Inflation Could Fuel Gold's Next Rally

Gold has fallen roughly $200 over the past two days and more than $2,000 from its 2026 record high, but Schiff believes the retreat could offer investors an opportunity rather than signal the end of the rally. Gold prices hit a high of $5,595 on Jan. 29, 2026.

He argued that gold's earlier surge was driven by concerns over rising federal debt and inflation, prompting central banks to reduce their exposure to the dollar and turn toward gold.

Schiff believes those forces are likely to intensify rather than fade, potentially setting the stage for another powerful move higher in gold.

"The reason gold hit that record was that rising federal debt & inflation caused central banks to flee the dollar in favor of gold," Schiff said.

"Debt & inflation will soon soar higher than ever," he added, urging investors to take advantage of gold's latest decline.

During the after-hours session on Friday, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), which tracks the S&P 500 index, gained 1.11%; the Invesco QQQ Trust ETF (QQQ) rose 1.53%; and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) surged 0.94%. Retail sentiment on Stocktwits toward the S&P 500 ETF was in the ‘bearish’ territory at the time of writing.

data.title: Hong Kong Bill Proposes HK$100,000 Fine for Unauthorized Crypto Titles, Two-Year Jail Term for Fake License Claims
data.description:
Hong Kong’s proposed virtual asset legislation would penalize unauthorized use of regulated service-provider titles and false claims of being a license applicant. According to Foresight News, citing Caixin, the 2026 Virtual Asset Service Legislation (Amendment) Bill introduces two offenses to address misleading promotions in the sector.

Anyone who is not licensed or registered but uses titles associated with virtual asset service providers regulated by the Securities and Futures Commission, such as “crypto trader,” “cryptocurrency adviser” or “virtual asset custodian,” could face a HK$100,000 fine upon conviction. Continuing violations would carry an additional HK$2,000 fine for each day they persist.

A person falsely claiming to be a license applicant could, upon conviction on indictment, face a HK$400,000 fine and up to two years in prison. Each day of a continuing offense could bring an additional HK$10,000 fine.

data.title: Dutch court bars Chinese SUV in Europe over resemblance to Land Rover Defender
data.description:
A Dutch district court in The Hague on Friday issued ​an injunction barring European Union sales of a large SUV made by China’s BYD, ‌saying it infringes on the design of Jaguar Land Rover’s popular Defender model.

JLR, ​a unit of India’s Tata Motors, launched the case earlier ⁠this year after BYD announced on its UK website that the seven-seater Ti7 SUV was available for orders with deliveries to customers starting in January 2027.

BYD launched the Fangchengbao Ti7 ‌in China last year.

The Defender is JLR’s most popular model, with global sales of over 100,000 units in 2025.

“In these summary proceedings, ‌the preliminary relief judge rules that the Ti7 infringes the EU design of ‌Jaguar ⁠Land Rover,” the court ruling said. “The characteristic and distinctive elements of the ⁠design are reflected in the BYD Ti7.”

According to automotive media, among the visual similarities between the two vehicles are a boxy, flat-roof silhouette, upright proportions, tailgate styling, squared-off wheel arches and a solid body-colored ​panel behind the rear passenger ‌door.

The injunction will take effect a week after the ruling because BYD “currently has no concrete plans to place the Ti7 on the market in the EU.”

Until the intellectual property case is resolved, the court also banned BYD from producing ‌the vehicle at its new factory in Hungary, which is due to ​start mass-producing cars early next year.

The judge ruled, however, that the court had no jurisdiction over BYD’s affiliate in the United Kingdom.

It ⁠is rare in Europe for major automakers to go to court over design rights infringement. It is also uncommon for such a ruling to come so early ‌in proceedings of a case that is ongoing and likely to last for some time.

“We protect our intellectual property and take legal action when necessary,” JLR said in a statement. “Legal proceedings are ongoing, and we won’t be commenting further at this time.”

Legacy automakers have often complained that Chinese automakers have copied designs, though little has been proven in court. In 2005, for instance, General Motors and Chinese ‌rival Chery settled a case over the Chery QQ that the No. 1 US automaker said was ​a copy of its Chevrolet Spark.

In a statement, BYD said it “strongly disagrees” with the ruling and will appeal it.

“The BYD Ti ⁠7 is the result of BYD’s own independent design work and infringes none of JLR’s ⁠rights,” BYD said. “We will pursue every legal avenue to demonstrate that this decision is incorrect.”

BYD has grown rapidly in Europe since launching sales on ‌the continent in late 2022. According to ACEA data, the Chinese automaker’s sales more than doubled to over 280,000 vehicles in Europe this year through September ​over the same period last year, outselling Ford, Tesla and Nissan.
